headline: Friday's panic is already being bought back — VIX -7.1%, Korea +1.8%, gasoline -11.7% on the month — but SKEW at a 52-week high and HYG/IEF at z=-1.26 say nobody actually sold any risk.
summary: The vol shock is deflating at the surface. VIX 18.57, -7.1% after Friday's +21% spike. KOSPI +1.8% following a -16.3% month (z=-2.35, acceleration z=-2.24, still the most extreme print on the tape). AUDUSD +1.0%, AUDJPY +1.0%, copper +0.9% to 6.591 at the 89th percentile, copper/gold at the 93rd. USDKRW -0.9% to 1,329 — the 0th percentile of its 52-week range, which is the single cleanest argument that the Asia tech unwind is positioning, not funding. And the oil tax I leaned on 24 hours ago is already deflating: WTI -2.7% to 98.65, Brent -0.8% to 108.95, RBOB -3.7% today and -11.7% on the month (z=-1.17, acc z=-1.25), with corn -10.3% and wheat -7.3% on the month. Risk regime -18 versus -17: the headline number didn't move, the composition did.

What did not repair is the hedging bid, and that is the day's real tension. SKEW is 168.59, z=2.24, acceleration z=1.23, the 100th percentile of its year — tail protection is being accumulated into a falling spot VIX. VIX/VIX3M is still 0.975, +16.8% on the week, a whisker from inversion. Spot vol down with skew and term structure stressed is distribution, not relief. Credit says the same thing from the other side: HYG -1.6% on the month at z=-1.04, HYG/IEF z=-1.26 and acc z=-0.98, BKLN z=-0.72 — junk spreads widened in a week IEF rallied 1.1% and the 10y fell 15bp. The equity tells are all in financing: BX -13.6% on the month at the 11th percentile, ORCL -10.1% and 19.4% below its 200-day at the 7th, GS -6.0%, KBE -4.2%, KRE/SPY at the 28th.

Rates remain the binding constraint; composite -56. 10y 5.09%, 30y 5.43%, 10y real 2.74% and 26.0% above its 200-day, MOVE 101.1 (+25.2% on the month, z=1.32). The long end did rally last week (-15bp on 10s, -17bp on 30s, TLT +2.7%) but 2s10s is only 35bp at the 28th percentile and breakevens ticked back up (5y +4bp to 2.37, 10y +3bp to 2.35) even as crude fell. The clearing price is housing: the 30-year mortgage is 7.40%, +64bp in a month, z=1.91, acceleration z=1.34, 100th percentile. XHB sits 9.6% below its 200-day at the 7.6th percentile, ITB at the 10th, XHB/SPY at the 6.5th, DHI at the 22nd. Nothing in the equity bounce touches that.

Leadership hasn't changed — it has hardened. XLV +5.7% on the month (z=1.27, 99th percentile, relative strength turning up), LLY +10.5%, UNH +7.0%, WMT +10.5% (acc z=1.72), COST +10.7%, XLP z=1.47, QUAL and USMV at the 93rd and 97th percentiles. Energy equity holds the 100th percentile — XLE +7.2% on the month, XOP at 100, XOM +9.6% and CVX +6.4% both at 52-week highs — on a day crude fell. The destruction is concentrated in everything levered to the AI-power buildout: NLR -12.1% month at the 0th percentile, URA -14.4% (0th), REMX -19.8% month and 36.3% below its 200-day (0th), LIT -8.3%, TAN -6.2% (0th), GRID -2.3%. And the loudest number in FX is USDMXN: +7.6% on the month, z=2.81, acc z=1.69, while the Mexican IPC is +8.5% (z=1.82), EWW +4.2% on the week and CEW is flat at -0.3%. That is an idiosyncratic peso problem, not EM risk-off.

good.text: The Asia unwind is positioning, not stress: KOSPI +1.8% after -16.3% on the month (z=-2.35), while USDKRW fell 0.9% to 1,329 — the 0th percentile of its 52-week range. A real outflow would show in the currency first.

The energy inflation tax is reversing: WTI -2.7% to 98.65, RBOB -3.7% today and -11.7% on the month (z=-1.17, acc z=-1.25), corn -10.3%, wheat -7.3%. The pump-price impulse that threatened the Fed path is fading.

Growth pulse intact where it matters: copper +0.9% to 6.591 (89th percentile), copper/gold +5.2% on the month at the 93rd, AUDUSD +1.0% and AUD/JPY +1.0%. Cyclical metals are not pricing a recession scare.
Defensive leadership with real earnings behind it keeps compounding: XLV +5.7% month (z=1.27, 99th percentile, RS turning up), LLY +10.5%, UNH +7.0%, WMT +10.5% (acc z=1.72), COST +10.7%, XLP z=1.47.

Breadth improved under a falling index: RSP/SPY +0.7% Friday and +2.5% on the week, equal-weight +0.5% while NDX was -5.5% and QQQ/SPY -3.6%. The de-rating is in crowded megacap tech, not the average stock.
The long end is doing its job: 10y -15bp on the week to 5.09%, 30y -17bp, 10y real -17bp, TLT +2.7%. Duration is finally hedging equity drawdowns again.

bad.text: Crash protection is being bought into a falling VIX: SKEW 168.59, z=2.24, acceleration z=1.23, 100th percentile, with VIX/VIX3M still 0.975 (+16.8% week). Spot vol down and tail vol up is the wrong combination for chasing this bounce.
Credit flatly refuses to ratify the rebound: HYG/IEF z=-1.26 and -1.6% on the month, HYG z=-1.04, BKLN z=-0.72 — spreads widened in a week Treasuries rallied 15bp.

Financing-sensitive equity is cracking first: BX -13.6% on the month at the 11th percentile, ORCL -10.1% and 19.4% below its 200-day at the 7th, GS -6.0%, KBE -4.2%, IAI -2.9%, KRE/SPY at the 28th percentile.

Mortgage rates are accelerating the wrong way: 7.40%, +64bp in a month, z=1.91, acc z=1.34, 100th percentile. XHB is 9.6% below its 200-day at the 7.6th percentile, ITB at the 10th, XHB/SPY at the 6.5th.

Rates composite -56 with bond vol still rising: MOVE 101.1 (+25.2% month, z=1.32), 30y 5.43%, 10y real 2.74% (26.0% above its 200-day), 2s10s only 35bp at the 28th percentile. Breakevens ticked up even with crude lower.

The AI-power and cyclical cohorts are in outright liquidation: NLR -12.1% month (0th percentile), URA -14.4% (0th), REMX -19.8% month and -36.3% vs its 200-day, TAN -6.2% (0th), plus IWM/SPY at the 7th percentile (z=-1.67) and JETS -7.0%.

trades.name: Short HYG vs long IEF
trades.line: Short HYG vs IEF: credit never bounced
trades.expr: Short $1 HYG against long $1 IEF, 2-3% of book; or buy HYG Dec 76 puts outright for convexity.
trades.thesis: High yield is the only market that did not participate in last week's Treasury rally, and the equity proxies for leveraged credit are already at 52-week-relative lows. If the vol shock is real, credit is where it settles; if it isn't, you pay carry, not capital.
trades.trigger: HYG/IEF at z=-1.26, -1.6% on the month, acceleration z=-0.98, with HYG -0.3% Friday and BKLN z=-0.72 — all deteriorating in a week IEF gained 1.1%. BX -13.6% and ORCL -10.1% on the month corroborate from the equity side.
trades.stop: HYG/IEF back above 0.865 (+1.8% from 0.850) or HYG reclaiming 78.
trades.target: HYG 74.5; ratio 0.825, roughly -3% on the pair.

trades.name: Short homebuilders (XHB/ITB)
trades.line: Short XHB: 7.40% mortgage, +64bp in one month
trades.expr: Short ITB outright, or buy XHB Jan 90/80 put spreads; pair against long SPY if you want it market-neutral.
trades.thesis: A 7.40% 30-year mortgage at the 100th percentile, rising 64bp in a month, cannot be bought down with incentives indefinitely. Gross margins compress before volumes do, and the group's relative line has already broken.
trades.trigger: MORTGAGE30US z=1.91 with acceleration z=1.34; XHB 9.6% below its 200-day at the 7.6th percentile; XHB/SPY at the 6.5th; ITB -10.5% over 3 months; DHI at the 22nd percentile — and the 10y is still 5.09%.
trades.stop: 30-year mortgage back below 7.00%, or XHB closing above 99 (its 200-day zone).

trades.name: Long XLE / short XLI
trades.line: Long XLE vs short XLI: 100th pctile vs rolling over
trades.expr: Dollar-neutral long XLE against short XLI; or express the long leg via XOM/CVX and short XLI against it.
trades.thesis: Energy is the only sector at the 100th percentile of its 52-week range with relative strength still rising, and it held that on a day crude fell 2.7% — cash flow, not spot oil, is driving it. Industrials are the mirror: rolling over, -8.9% relative over three months.
trades.trigger: XLE +7.2% on the month with RS +5.7%/+15.6% and state 'up'; XOM +9.6% and CVX +6.4%, both at 52-week highs; XOP at the 100th percentile. Against that, XLI RS 'down', XLI/XLU -3.1% on the month, CAT -16.8% and GEV -12.9% over 3 months.
trades.stop: Brent below 98 (round-tripping the month's +4.9%), or XLE 1m relative strength turning negative.

trades.name: Long Korea (EWY)
trades.line: Long EWY: -16% month, z=-2.35, won at 52wk strong
trades.expr: Long EWY, or KOSPI futures; hedge the beta with a partial SMH short if you only want the Asia-vs-US-semi relative.
trades.thesis: A -16.3% monthly drawdown at z=-2.35 with acceleration z=-2.24 is capitulation, not a slow de-rating, and the currency refuses to confirm distress. When the exchange rate is at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range (i.e. strongest) during an equity rout, you are looking at a de-grossing, not an exit.
trades.trigger: KOSPI +1.8% today, the first up day of the unwind; USDKRW -0.9% to 1,329 and -3.7% on the month; Taiwan stabilising at -0.6% and still 15.1% above its 200-day. EWY is -14.3% on the month but only 6.1% below its own 200-day.
trades.stop: USDKRW back above 1,380, or EWY closing below 140.
trades.target: EWY 168 — half the month's drop retraced.

trades.name: SPX downside while spot vol cheapens
trades.line: Buy Dec SPX put spreads while VIX dips to 18.6
trades.expr: Buy SPX Dec 7,300/6,800 put spreads, partly financed by selling a 1-month 8,000 call; or Dec VIX 25 calls for the pure convexity version.
trades.thesis: Buy the hedge when spot vol is giving back the spike but the tail bid is at an annual extreme. The index is still 5.3% above its 200-day near 7,270, so there is room to the first real support, and the vol surface says professionals are paying up for exactly that path.
trades.trigger: VIX -7.1% to 18.57 after Friday's +21% while SKEW prints 168.59 (z=2.24, acc z=1.23, 100th percentile) and VIX/VIX3M stays at 0.975, +16.8% on the week. Spot vol down, tail vol up.
trades.stop: VIX/VIX3M back below 0.90 with SKEW under 155 — the tail bid has cleared, take the premium loss.

trades.name: Long Brazil (EWZ)
trades.line: Long EWZ: +11.6% month, best RS on the tape
trades.expr: Long EWZ; add Jan 44 calls for upside convexity. Keep it unhedged on FX — the real is part of the thesis.
trades.thesis: Brazil is the only market in the digest with positive, rising relative strength and a firming currency simultaneously. Commodity-heavy index, falling USD/BRL, and a local equity market at the 89th percentile while the EM complex rolls over.
trades.trigger: BVSP +10.7% on the month (z=1.80), EWZ +11.6% (z=1.29) with RS +10.0% on the month and turning up; USDBRL -1.0% on the month and -7.4% ytd, rolling over. Meanwhile EEM/SPY is z=-1.39 and rolling over — Brazil is decoupling from EM, not riding it.

trades.name: Short USDMXN
trades.line: Short USDMXN: z=2.81 blowout, equities disagree
trades.expr: Short USDMXN in forwards, 1-2% risk budget; or buy 3-month USDMXN puts to cap the tail if this is a policy/fiscal event rather than a flow unwind.
trades.thesis: A 7.6% monthly move at z=2.81 with acceleration z=1.69 is the most extreme reading in the entire digest, and nothing around it corroborates: CEW is -0.3% on the month, USDBRL -1.0%, USDKRW -3.7%. Mexican equities are making highs, not discounting a shock.
trades.trigger: USDMXN 18.47, 5.9% above its 200-day at the 89th percentile, but the move is decelerating to +0.2% today — while the IPC is +8.5% on the month (z=1.82, acc z=1.61) and EWW +4.2% on the week.
